about: SYNTHETIC content for tests and the retrieval eval (T-AGT-03, D-94). Written for this repo; not from the Live Well book or any copyrighted source. Driver keys are provisional (needs-product). reviewed_by is a placeholder. Items whose id starts with pending_/retired_/rejected_/draft_/expired_ are deliberately on-topic distractors that must never be retrieved.

items.title: A short walk after meals
cards: A gentle walk after a meal is one of the easiest ways to move more during the day.
Start with five minutes at an easy pace. You should be able to talk while you walk.
Pick one meal, like lunch, and pair your walk with it so it becomes a habit.
On busy days a slow walk around the house or office still counts.

microhabit.title: Walk for five minutes after lunch

items.title: Stretch breaks at your desk
cards: Sitting for long hours makes the body feel stiff. Short stretch breaks help you move more.
Stand up, roll your shoulders back and reach your arms up slowly.
Stretch only as far as feels good. Gentle movement is the goal, never pain.
Set a reminder to stand and stretch every hour while you work.

microhabit.title: Stand and stretch once every hour

items.title: Movement in everyday life
sections: Movement does not have to mean a gym. Walking to the shop, taking the stairs and stretching while the kettle boils all add up across a day.
Begin small. A few minutes of easy walking that you repeat every day matters more than one long, hard workout that you never repeat.
Choose movement you enjoy, such as dancing in the kitchen, gardening or a walk with a friend, so moving more feels like a gift and not a chore.

items.title: A calm wind-down before bed
cards: A regular wind-down routine tells your body it is time to sleep.
Dim the lights and put screens away about thirty minutes before bed.
Try a warm shower, light reading or slow breathing to relax.
Going to bed at the same time each night helps you fall asleep more easily.

microhabit.title: Screens off thirty minutes before bed

items.title: Make your bedroom sleep friendly
cards: A cool, dark and quiet bedroom makes it easier to sleep through the night.
Use curtains or an eye mask to block light, and keep the room comfortably cool.
Keep the bed for sleep and rest, not for work or scrolling on your phone.
If you cannot fall asleep after a while, get up, do something calm and return when sleepy.

microhabit.title: Charge your phone outside the bedroom tonight

items.title: Sleep and your daily rhythm
sections: Your body likes rhythm. Waking up and going to bed at about the same time every day, even at weekends, helps your sleep feel deeper and more restful.
Morning daylight helps set your body clock. A few minutes outside after waking can make it easier to feel sleepy at night.
Heavy meals and caffeine late in the evening can keep you awake. A lighter evening and a calm bedtime routine support good sleep.

items.title: Add a vegetable to every meal
cards: Eating more vegetables is a simple way to eat better without strict rules.
Add one vegetable to a meal you already eat, like spinach in an omelette or carrots with lunch.
Fill half your plate with colourful vegetables when you can.
Frozen vegetables are quick, cheap and just as good for busy days.

microhabit.title: Add one vegetable to dinner today

items.title: Eat slowly and enjoy your food
cards: Eating slowly helps you notice when you are full and enjoy your meal more.
Sit down to eat, away from screens, and take a breath before your first bite.
Put your fork down between bites and chew your food well.
Notice the taste, colour and smell of your food. Meals are a time to slow down.

microhabit.title: Eat one meal today without a screen

items.title: Building a balanced plate
sections: A balanced plate has vegetables, whole grains and a source of protein such as lentils, beans, eggs, fish or paneer. Simple home cooked meals make it easier to eat well.
Drinking water through the day and choosing whole fruit over sweet drinks are small food habits that are easy to keep.
Eating better is about adding good foods, not about strict diets. Small changes to the meals you already enjoy last longer.

items.title: Slow breathing for stressful moments
cards: When you feel stressed, slow breathing can help your body calm down.
Breathe in gently through your nose for a count of four, then breathe out slowly for six.
Repeat for one or two minutes. Let your shoulders drop as you breathe out.
You can use slow breathing anywhere: before a meeting, in traffic or before sleep.

microhabit.title: Take one minute of slow breathing at lunch

items.title: Put your worries on paper
cards: Worries can feel smaller when you write them down instead of carrying them in your head.
Set aside ten minutes a day as worry time. Write each worry and one small step you could take.
When a worry comes back later, remind yourself it has a place in tomorrow's worry time.
Writing things down can lower stress and help you feel more in control.

microhabit.title: Write down one worry and one small step

items.title: The power of a pause
sections: Stress is a normal part of life, but long stretches of stress without rest wear us down. Short pauses during the day help the body and mind recover.
A pause can be three slow breaths, a stretch, a cup of tea in silence or a short walk outside. What matters is that you step away for a moment.
Notice your early signs of stress, such as tight shoulders or a racing mind, and use them as a signal to pause and breathe.

items.title: Beat the afternoon energy slump
cards: Many people feel tired and low on energy in the afternoon.
Instead of another coffee, try a glass of water and a short walk to lift your energy.
Natural light and fresh air can help you feel more awake and alert.
A lighter lunch with vegetables and protein can keep your energy steadier.

microhabit.title: Drink a glass of water at three o'clock

items.title: Start the morning with energy
cards: How you start your morning can shape your energy for the whole day.
Open the curtains for daylight and drink a glass of water soon after waking.
A few minutes of gentle movement in the morning helps you feel more awake.
A simple breakfast gives your body fuel and steady energy until lunch.

microhabit.title: Open the curtains and drink water after waking

items.title: Where your energy comes from
sections: Energy comes from many small things: sleep, food, movement, water and rest. When you feel tired, look at these everyday sources first.
Short breaks across the day protect your energy. Pushing on without rest often leaves you drained by evening.
Notice the activities and people that give you energy and those that take it away, and plan your day to include more of what lifts you.

items.title: Stack a new habit on an old one
cards: A new habit is easier to keep when you link it to something you already do every day.
Use the pattern: after I brush my teeth, I will stretch for two minutes.
Pick an anchor that happens at the same time each day, like your morning tea.
Keep the new habit tiny at first so it is easy to repeat, even on hard days.

microhabit.title: Pick one anchor for a two minute habit

items.title: Plan tomorrow the night before
cards: A simple daily routine makes healthy habits feel automatic.
Each evening, write down the three most important things for tomorrow.
Put your healthy habit, like a walk or a glass of water, at a fixed time in your daily plan.
A steady routine lowers the number of decisions you need to make each day.

microhabit.title: Write three things to do tomorrow

items.title: Small habits, done daily
sections: Habits grow through repetition. Doing a small action at the same time every day matters more than doing a big action once in a while.
When you miss a day, simply start again the next day. One missed day does not break a habit; giving up does.
Write your daily routine where you can see it and tick off each habit as you complete it. Seeing progress keeps you going.

items.title: Reach out to someone you care about
cards: Feeling connected to other people is an important part of living well.
Call or message a friend or family member you have not spoken to in a while.
Ask how they are and really listen. Short conversations still build strong bonds.
Make it a weekly habit to reach out to one person you care about.

microhabit.title: Send a kind message to one friend today

items.title: Share a meal with family
cards: Eating together is a simple way to feel closer to family and friends.
Plan one shared meal this week, at home or with neighbours.
Put phones away at the table and talk about the best part of your day.
Shared meals help everyone slow down, connect and enjoy their food.

microhabit.title: Plan one family meal this week

items.title: Belonging and community
sections: People who feel they belong to a family, group or community often find it easier to keep healthy habits. Friends and family can encourage us on hard days.
Join a walking group, a class or a place of worship, or volunteer in your neighbourhood. Shared activities create friendships over time.
Loneliness is common and nothing to be ashamed of. Reaching out to one person is a brave and healthy first step.

items.title: A daily gratitude moment
cards: Noticing what is going well can lift your mood and build a more hopeful mindset.
Each night, write down three good things that happened today, however small.
They can be simple: a warm cup of tea, a kind word or a sunny walk.
Over time, a gratitude habit trains your mind to notice the good in each day.

microhabit.title: Write three good things before bed

items.title: Talk to yourself like a friend
cards: The way you talk to yourself shapes how you feel and act.
When you slip up, notice harsh self talk and ask what you would say to a friend.
Replace 'I always fail' with 'I am learning, and I can try again tomorrow'.
Kind self talk keeps you going when change feels hard.

microhabit.title: Say one kind sentence to yourself today

items.title: A hopeful mindset
sections: Change starts with a hopeful mindset: believing that small steps can make a difference in how you feel each day.
Celebrate small wins. Every walk, glass of water or early night is progress worth noticing and enjoying.
Setbacks are part of every journey. A kind and curious mindset helps you learn from a hard day instead of giving up.

items.title: Eat well from an Indian kitchen
cards: Dal, sabzi and roti or rice make a balanced everyday plate.
Add a bowl of curd or a salad of cucumber and tomato to lunch.
Choose roasted snacks like chana over fried ones most days.

microhabit.title: Add a salad to lunch

items.title: Pending: sleep tips
cards: Sleep better tonight: a wind-down routine before bed, screens off, dim lights, same bedtime, calm sleep.
Sleep sleep sleep: bedroom dark and cool for deep sleep and falling asleep easily.

microhabit.title: Go to bed early

items.title: Retired: walking plan
cards: Walk after meals every day. A short walk after lunch at an easy pace helps you move more.
Walking walking walking: take a gentle walk after each meal.

microhabit.title: Walk after each meal

items.title: Rejected: stress
cards: Slow breathing for stress: breathe in for four and out for six whenever you feel stressed, to calm down.

microhabit.title: Breathe slowly

items.title: Draft: energy
cards: Afternoon energy slump? Drink water, take a short walk, get daylight to lift your energy.

microhabit.title: Drink water

items.title: Expired: vegetables
sections: Add a vegetable to every meal. Fill half your plate with colourful vegetables to eat better.
